findings.reason: §13 must add `tests/test_mcp_server_serves_current_code.py` to its write paths and state that its signature fixture becomes a removal or a new required parameter, or the node cannot satisfy its own "adds no failure" clause and stops blocked on a file it may not edit.
findings.text: §13 states `tests/test_mcp_server_serves_current_code.py` "adds no failure", but that file's `_SIGNATURE` fixture (tests/test_mcp_server_serves_current_code.py:96-101) changes the tool by `async def _edit_plan_tool(*args, added_parameter=None, **kwargs)` — an added optional parameter, which is exactly the change §13 makes compatible and serves with a `schema_note`. `test_a_changed_tool_signature_returns_the_reconnect_refusal` (:374) asserts `second.get("error") == "stale_server_code"` and would therefore fail, and the file is absent from §13's write paths, so the node meets a red test it is fenced out of and must stop blocked. The plan already knows this pattern: §13 handles the identical fixture in `tests/test_a_slow_child_never_forces_a_reconnect.py` ("whose changed-signature case becomes a removal", :327; its case 6 reports `added_parameter` at that file's :435)

findings.reason: a node implementing the rule literally ships a compatibility rule that admits a requiredness tightening and silently breaks client calls, so the clause and a probe payload of registered requiredness must be added, plus a fourth signature case.
findings.text: the deliverable's rule reads "A change is compatible when every registered parameter is still accepted and no new parameter is required", which passes a change that makes an existing registered optional parameter required: it is still accepted, and it is not new. Such a change invalidates a call the client can currently make (one that omits the parameter), so it breaks the principle the section argues from — "An added optional parameter leaves every call the client can make valid on the new code" (:305) — and the done-when's three signature cases (`:317-319`, added-optional / removed / new-required) contain no case for it. The probe already carries the data: "reports each tool's parameters with whether each one is required" (`:309`), so the parent could send its registered requiredness and the child could catch the transition
